Today is the ten year anniversary of the horror game that changed indie horror forever, as well as changed the lives of many people too. This game also bumped a lot of YouTubers up in popularity as well, and even for some it might've been the entire base for their whole channel. If somehow you haven't played this game or maybe you aren't a fan of this genre, I would still highly recommend giving this game a chance. I believe that this game should be played at least once by anyone who is a horror game fan, or just a video game fan in general. Thank you Scott for changing indie horror as we know it today, and changing the lives of many fans too.

An extremely scary game. If you own steam, maybe this scary game is just worth trying. It definitely doesn't give you much info at the start, it mainly just allows you to understand your a night guard at a children's pizzeria with animatronic birthday party shows and an odd need to have somebody watch them during the night. If the story isn't the best, then this games gameplay is the main reason to buy it, I won't spoil it since its a key part of the game but I appreciate that it allows the player to learn rather than having a quick tutorial pop up on the screen, it's a great way to scare the player rather than just telling them to do that to avoid getting scared. I highly recommend this game.

If you're looking to buy Five Nights at Freddy's as a horror game, I'm going to tell you that you might be disappointed. To me, the game's only scary if you play it in the dark. Otherwise, it's not too spooky.
If you're looking to get this game as a fun experience, I still suggest you get this game. What this game lacks in scares it accounts for in exciting gameplay. While dealing with four killer animatronics while conserving battery power isn't as scary as it sounds, it is quite a challenging experience, and a fun one at that.
Either way, Five Nights at Freddy's isn't a scary game, but it's still a thrill for anyone who likes kicking back, relaxing, and trying to keep an animatronic bear from leaping out at them. Either that, or a fan of the strategy genre.

Took me a while to jump on the FNAF bandwagon but I'm so glad I did. The OG FNAF is very simplistic in terms of graphics and gameplay but incredibly challenging and addictive. Plenty of jumpscares, a learning curve to work those brain muscles, and an excellent introduction to the FNAF world for those just jumping on the bandwagon, like me.

Pros
- Challenging but satisfying gameplay
- Surprisingly addictive
- Excellent introduction to the series and characters

Cons
- Simplistic gameplay
- Basic graphics
- Jumpscares can be a little cheesy
- Hard to understand what you're supposed to do at points

Overall Rating: 7.5/10

An awesome little click-and-point indie game (with quite a reputation at this point) that never ceases to heighten my stress levels.
I finally got around to playing this series, and the original Five Nights at Freddy's is an excellent reminder of how a simple idea with key components can create a huge franchise.

The game is excellent as a strategy game as you race against the clock amd Chica, Bonnie, Freddy, and Foxy. The graphics, at the time, were good. And the jump scares are just awesome; although, they do become predictable and uninteresting by the time you finish the game. But tell me a game that doesn't run into that issue in the horror genre?

I'd highly recommend this game if you want a good, fun thrill that doesn't involve excessive commitment.
